revealWordProblem.title: Apply: The Louvre Pyramid
revealWordProblem.text: The Louvre Pyramid in Paris is a square pyramid made of glass panels. How could you use a net and the surface area formula to find the total area of glass in its four triangular faces?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Unfold the pyramid into a net: the square base separates from the four triangular faces so each one lies flat and can be measured on its own. Since the question only asks about the glass in the four triangular faces, find the area of one triangular face using ½ × base edge × slant height, then multiply by 4 — the base square is not part of this total. For example, if the base edge is 6 ft and the slant height is 8 ft, one triangular face is ½ × 6 × 8 = 24 ft², so the four faces together need 4 × 24 = 96 ft² of glass.

conceptIntro.heading: How do we find the surface area of a pyramid?
conceptIntro.intro: Surface area of a pyramid is the base area plus all the triangular side faces. A square pyramid has 1 square base and 4 triangular faces. Each triangle uses the slant height: ½ × base × slant height.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Surface area of a pyramid = base area + the area of all the triangular lateral faces.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: My square pyramid has a 6 in. × 6 in. base and a slant height of 8 in.
Now one triangular face: ½ × 6 × 8 = 24. A square pyramid has 4 of them, so 4 × 24 = 96.
I add the base and the side faces: 36 + 96 = 132.
So the total surface area is 132 in². I used the slant height (8) for the triangles, not the pyramid's height.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: Now a smaller square pyramid: base 4 × 4, slant height 5. What is the base area?
Right, 4 × 4 = 16. Now one triangular face: ½ × 4 × 5. What do you get?
Yes, 10. Four faces is 4 × 10 = 40. Now add the base: 16 + 40. What is the surface area?
Yes, SA = 56 in². Don't forget to add the base area!

Remember: total SA = base area + all the triangular faces.

optionalActivity.name: Pyramid Gift Box Designer
optionalActivity.intro: Design pyramid-shaped gift boxes for the time capsule and figure out exactly how much wrapping paper covers every face.

optional.stem: Your first gift box is a square pyramid with a base edge of 7 in and a slant height of 9 in. How much wrapping paper (total surface area) covers it?
optional.explanation: Base: 7 × 7 = 49 in². One triangular face: ½ × 7 × 9 = 31.5 in². Four faces: 4 × 31.5 = 126 in². SA = 49 + 126 = 175 in². Surface area uses square units (in²).
choiceFeedback: You found the four triangular faces but forgot to add the square base.
Recalculate the base area (side × side) and each triangular face separately before adding.
Check the units — wrapping paper covers a surface, so it needs square units, not cubic.
optional.stemEs: Tu primera caja de regalo es una pirámide cuadrada con una arista de base de 7 in y una altura inclinada de 9 in. ¿Cuánto papel de regalo (área de superficie total) la cubre?
optional.explanationEs: Base: 7 × 7 = 49 in². Una cara triangular: ½ × 7 × 9 = 31.5 in². Cuatro caras: 4 × 31.5 = 126 in². Área de superficie = 49 + 126 = 175 in². El área de superficie usa unidades cuadradas (in²).
hints: Wrapping paper has to cover every face you could touch: the square base plus all four triangles.
Find the base area first, then the area of one triangular face, then multiply that face by how many lateral faces there are before you add.
Start with the base: 7 × 7 = 49 in². One triangular face is ½ × 7 × 9 = 31.5 in². How many of those triangles are there, and what do you still add?
hintsEs: El papel de regalo tiene que cubrir todas las caras que puedes tocar: la base cuadrada más las cuatro caras triangulares.
Halla primero el área de la base, luego el área de una cara triangular, y después multiplica esa cara por el número de caras laterales antes de sumar.
Empieza con la base: 7 × 7 = 49 in². Una cara triangular es ½ × 7 × 9 = 31.5 in². ¿Cuántos triángulos como ese hay, y qué te falta sumar?

optional.stem: Before adding the base, you need the area of just one triangular face of a gift box with base edge 8 in and slant height 5 in. What is it?
optional.explanation: Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height = ½ × 8 × 5 = 20 in². You use the slant height (5) as the triangle's height, not the pyramid's vertical height.
choiceFeedback: Don't forget to take half — a triangle's area is half of base times height.
Adding the base and height together won't give area — multiply them, then take half.
Check the units — a flat triangular face is measured in square units, not cubic.
optional.stemEs: Antes de sumar la base, necesitas el área de una sola cara triangular de una caja de regalo con arista de base de 8 in y altura inclinada de 5 in. ¿Cuál es?
optional.explanationEs: Área de un triángulo = ½ × base × altura = ½ × 8 × 5 = 20 in². Usas la altura inclinada (5) como altura del triángulo, no la altura vertical de la pirámide.
hints: A lateral face of a pyramid is a triangle, and a triangle's area is half of base × height.
The slant height acts as the triangle's height here, and the square base is not part of this step at all.
Multiply base × slant height first: 8 × 5 = 40. A triangle covers only half of that rectangle — finish the last step.
hintsEs: Una cara lateral de una pirámide es un triángulo, y el área de un triángulo es la mitad de base × altura.
Aquí la altura inclinada funciona como la altura del triángulo, y la base cuadrada no entra en este paso.
Multiplica primero base × altura inclinada: 8 × 5 = 40. Un triángulo cubre solo la mitad de ese rectángulo: termina el último paso.

optional.stem: A gift box is a square pyramid with a base edge of 9 in. What is the area of its square base (the part that sits on the table)?
optional.explanation: The base is a square, so base area = side × side = 9 × 9 = 81 in². You would still add the four triangular faces to get the full surface area.
choiceFeedback: That looks like a perimeter calculation — area of a square is side × side, not side × 4.
Doubling the side length isn't the same as squaring it — multiply the side by itself.
That includes extra faces — the base area alone only needs side × side, not four times that.
optional.stemEs: Una caja de regalo es una pirámide cuadrada con una arista de base de 9 in. ¿Cuál es el área de su base cuadrada (la parte que se apoya en la mesa)?
optional.explanationEs: La base es un cuadrado, así que el área de la base = lado × lado = 9 × 9 = 81 in². Todavía tendrías que sumar las cuatro caras triangulares para obtener el área de superficie total.
hints: The base of a square pyramid is a square, and every side of a square has the same length.
The area of a square is side × side, so no slant height is needed for this part.
Both sides of the base measure 9 in, so set up 9 × 9 and compute it.
hintsEs: La base de una pirámide cuadrada es un cuadrado, y todos los lados de un cuadrado miden lo mismo.
El área de un cuadrado es lado × lado, así que no se necesita la altura inclinada en esta parte.
Los dos lados de la base miden 9 in, así que plantea 9 × 9 y calcúlalo.

optional.label: Match each square-pyramid gift box (base edge × slant height) to its total surface area.
optional.hint: Add the base area and the four triangular faces to find each total surface area.
optional.explanation: Each box's total is its square base plus four triangles: 25 + 4(20) = 105 in², 36 + 4(21) = 120 in², 64 + 4(36) = 208 in², and 100 + 4(30) = 220 in². Notice the last two are close in total even though their shapes differ — you have to compute both parts rather than judging by the base edge alone.
optional.explanationEs: El total de cada caja es su base cuadrada más cuatro triángulos: 25 + 4(20) = 105 in², 36 + 4(21) = 120 in², 64 + 4(36) = 208 in² y 100 + 4(30) = 220 in². Fíjate en que los dos últimos totales quedan cerca aunque las formas son distintas: hay que calcular las dos partes en vez de juzgar solo por la arista de la base.
optional.labelEs: Une cada caja de regalo con forma de pirámide cuadrada (arista de la base × altura inclinada) con su área superficial total.

optional.correctWork: Each triangular face uses the base edge (12) as its base and the slant height (9) as its height: ½ × 12 × 9 = 54 in². The student used the slant height (9) in place of the base edge by mistake. Four faces: 4 × 54 = 216 in². Correct SA = 144 + 216 = 360 in².

optional.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2 — Altura inclinada contra arista de la base
optional.explanation: The face step used 9 twice, but a lateral triangle takes its base from the base edge (12 in) and its height from the slant height (9 in), so each face is ½ × 12 × 9 = 54 in², not 40.5 in². Four faces give 216 in², and the correct total is SA = 144 + 216 = 360 in².
optional.explanationEs: El paso de la cara usó 9 dos veces, pero un triángulo lateral toma su base de la arista de la base (12 in) y su altura de la altura inclinada (9 in), así que cada cara es ½ × 12 × 9 = 54 in², no 40.5 in². Cuatro caras dan 216 in², y el total correcto es SA = 144 + 216 = 360 in².
optional.correctWorkEs: Cada cara triangular usa la arista de la base (12) como base y la altura inclinada (9) como altura: ½ × 12 × 9 = 54 in². El estudiante usó la altura inclinada (9) en lugar de la arista de la base por error. Cuatro caras: 4 × 54 = 216 in². SA correcta = 144 + 216 = 360 in².

question.stem: How many faces do you add together to find the surface area of this pyramid?

approaching.stem: A square pyramid has a base edge of 5 in and a slant height of 7 in. What is the surface area?
approaching.explanation: Base: 5 × 5 = 25 in². Each lateral face: ½ × 5 × 7 = 17.5 in². Four faces: 4 × 17.5 = 70 in². SA = 25 + 70 = 95 in².
choiceFeedback: You calculated the four triangular faces but forgot to add the square base area.
Check the units — surface area is measured in square units, not cubic.
Recheck each triangular face area — make sure you take half of base times slant height for each.
hints: A square pyramid has TWO kinds of faces: one square base (5 × 5) and four identical triangles with slant height 7.
SA = base area + 4 triangle areas, where each triangle is ½ × base edge × slant height.
Base first: 5 × 5 = 25 in². Then one triangle: ½ × 5 × 7. Multiply that by 4 and add the base area.
approaching.stemEs: Una pirámide cuadrada tiene una arista de base de 5 in y una altura inclinada de 7 in. ¿Cuál es el área de superficie?
approaching.explanationEs: Base: 5 × 5 = 25 in². Cada cara lateral: ½ × 5 × 7 = 17.5 in². Cuatro caras: 4 × 17.5 = 70 in². Área de superficie = 25 + 70 = 95 in².
hintsEs: Una pirámide cuadrangular tiene DOS tipos de caras: una base cuadrada (5 × 5) y cuatro triángulos idénticos con apotema de 7.
AS = área de la base + 4 áreas de triángulo, donde cada triángulo es ½ × arista de la base × apotema.
La base primero: 5 × 5 = 25 pulg². Luego un triángulo: ½ × 5 × 7. Multiplica eso por 4 y súmale el área de la base.

approaching.stem: How many lateral (triangular) faces does a square pyramid have?
approaching.explanation: A square pyramid has a square base and 4 triangular lateral faces — one for each side of the square.
choiceFeedback: A square base has four sides — count a triangular face for each side of the square.
The square base isn't a lateral (triangular) face — only count the slanted triangle sides.
That's too many — count only the slanted triangular sides around the square base.
hints: Lateral faces are the slanted triangles on the sides — the square base itself doesn't count.
Each side of the square base holds up exactly one triangle. Count the sides of a square.
Trace the base: it's a square. Count one triangle leaning against each side of that square.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuántas caras laterales (triangulares) tiene una pirámide cuadrada?
approaching.explanationEs: Una pirámide cuadrada tiene una base cuadrada y 4 caras laterales triangulares, una por cada lado del cuadrado.
hintsEs: Las caras laterales son los triángulos inclinados de los lados; la base cuadrada no cuenta.
Cada lado de la base cuadrada sostiene exactamente un triángulo. Cuenta los lados de un cuadrado.
Traza la base: es un cuadrado. Cuenta un triángulo apoyado en cada lado de ese cuadrado.

approaching.stem: What is the area of one triangular face with base 8 in and slant height 6 in?
approaching.explanation: Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height = ½ × 8 × 6 = 24 in².
choiceFeedback: Don't forget to take half — a triangle's area is half of base times height, not the full product.
Adding the base and height won't give area — multiply them first, then take half.
Check the units — a flat triangular face needs square units, not cubic.
hints: You have one triangle: base 8 in, slant height 6 in. Triangle area is not just base × height.
Use area = ½ × base × height — multiply the two numbers first, then take half.
Multiply 8 × 6 = 48 first. Then take half of that result.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el área de una cara triangular con base de 8 in y altura inclinada de 6 in?
approaching.explanationEs: Área de un triángulo = ½ × base × altura = ½ × 8 × 6 = 24 in².
hintsEs: Tienes un triángulo: base 8 pulg, apotema 6 pulg. El área del triángulo no es solo base × altura.
Usa área = ½ × base × altura: multiplica primero los dos números y luego saca la mitad.
Multiplica 8 × 6 = 48 primero. Luego saca la mitad de ese resultado.

approaching.instructions: Find the area of one lateral face for each pyramid.
approaching.hint: Use ½ × base edge × slant height to find each triangular face.
hints: Each row asks for the area of ONE triangular face, using its base edge and slant height.
Use ½ × base edge × slant height for each row — multiply the two numbers, then halve.
Pyramid 1: multiply 4 × 9 = 36, then take half. Write the result with in².
approaching.explanation: Every lateral face of a pyramid is a triangle whose base is the base edge and whose height is the slant height, so its area is ½ × base edge × slant height. That gives ½ × 4 × 9 = 18 in² for Pyramid 1, ½ × 6 × 5 = 15 cm² for Pyramid 2, and ½ × 10 × 8 = 40 ft² for Pyramid 3.
approaching.explanationEs: Cada cara lateral de una pirámide es un triángulo cuya base es la arista de la base y cuya altura es la altura inclinada, así que su área es ½ × arista de la base × altura inclinada. Eso da ½ × 4 × 9 = 18 in² para la Pirámide 1, ½ × 6 × 5 = 15 cm² para la Pirámide 2 y ½ × 10 × 8 = 40 ft² para la Pirámide 3.
approaching.instructionsEs: Encuentra el área de una cara lateral de cada pirámide.
hintsEs: Cada fila pide el área de UNA cara triangular, usando su arista de la base y su apotema.
Usa ½ × arista de la base × apotema en cada fila: multiplica los dos números y luego saca la mitad.
Pirámide 1: multiplica 4 × 9 = 36 y luego saca la mitad. Escribe el resultado con pulg².

approaching.label: Put the steps in order for finding the surface area of a square pyramid (base edge 6, slant height 10).
approaching.hint: Think about the order of steps for finding a pyramid's surface area.
hints: The cards walk from base area to lateral faces to the final total for a base-6, slant-10 pyramid.
Order: base area, then one triangle, then all four triangles, then add base + lateral, then state SA.
Place 'Find base area: 6 × 6 = 36' first — the base is your starting block before the triangles.
approaching.explanation: The steps follow the structure of the pyramid itself: find the square base (6 × 6 = 36), find one triangular face (½ × 6 × 10 = 30), multiply by the 4 faces (4 × 30 = 120), add base plus lateral (36 + 120), and state the total, SA = 156 in². The lateral total has to be built before it can be added to the base, so the order cannot be shuffled.
approaching.explanationEs: Los pasos siguen la estructura misma de la pirámide: halla la base cuadrada (6 × 6 = 36), halla una cara triangular (½ × 6 × 10 = 30), multiplica por las 4 caras (4 × 30 = 120), suma base más lateral (36 + 120) y escribe el total, SA = 156 in². El total lateral debe construirse antes de sumarlo a la base, así que el orden no se puede cambiar.
approaching.labelEs: Ordena los pasos para encontrar el área superficial de una pirámide cuadrada (arista de la base 6, altura inclinada 10).
hintsEs: Las tarjetas van del área de la base a las caras laterales y al total final para una pirámide de base 6 y apotema 10.
Orden: área de la base, luego un triángulo, luego los cuatro triángulos, luego suma base + laterales y luego da el AS.
Coloca 'Halla el área de la base: 6 × 6 = 36' primero: la base es tu bloque inicial antes de los triángulos.

approaching.title: Don't Forget the Base

workedExample.label: Box
workedExample.work: Square pyramid: base edge = 5 in, slant height = 6 in
workedExample.workEs: Pirámide cuadrada: arista de la base = 5 pulg, altura inclinada = 6 pulg

workedExample.label: Answer
workedExample.work: SA = 60 in² (stopped after the four triangular faces)
workedExample.workEs: SA = 60 in² (se detuvo después de las cuatro caras triangulares)

approaching.correctWork: The student found the lateral area (60 in²) but forgot to add the base. Base area = 5 × 5 = 25 in². Correct SA = base + lateral = 25 + 60 = 85 in².
hints: Did the student include the bottom of the pyramid?
Surface area = base area + lateral area. Add the base: 25 + 60 = 85 in².
approaching.explanation: The triangle work is right — each face is ½ × 5 × 6 = 15 in² and four faces give 60 in² — but the answer stops at the lateral area. Surface area covers the whole solid, so the 5 × 5 = 25 in² square base still has to be added, making SA = 25 + 60 = 85 in².
approaching.explanationEs: El trabajo con los triángulos está bien —cada cara es ½ × 5 × 6 = 15 in² y cuatro caras dan 60 in²— pero la respuesta se detiene en el área lateral. El área total cubre todo el cuerpo, así que todavía hay que sumar la base cuadrada de 5 × 5 = 25 in², de modo que SA = 25 + 60 = 85 in².
approaching.correctWorkEs: El estudiante encontró el área lateral (60 in²) pero olvidó sumar la base. Área de la base = 5 × 5 = 25 in². SA correcta = base + lateral = 25 + 60 = 85 in².

onLevel.instructions: Find the surface area of each square pyramid.
onLevel.hint: Use base area + 4 × (½ × base edge × slant height) for each row.
hints: Each row needs two answers: the square base's area, then the TOTAL surface area (base + 4 triangles).
Base area = edge × edge. Then add 4 × (½ × edge × slant height) for the four triangular faces.
Pyramid X: base area is 12 × 12. Each triangle is ½ × 12 × 10 — find that, multiply by 4, and add to the base.
onLevel.explanation: Each row is base area plus four triangular faces: Pyramid X gives 12 × 12 = 144 in² plus 4 × (½ × 12 × 10) = 240 in², so SA = 384 in². The same plan gives Pyramid Y 64 cm² + 4 × 24 = 160 cm² and Pyramid Z 196 ft² + 4 × 77 = 504 ft².
onLevel.explanationEs: Cada fila es el área de la base más cuatro caras triangulares: la Pirámide X da 12 × 12 = 144 in² más 4 × (½ × 12 × 10) = 240 in², así que SA = 384 in². El mismo plan da para la Pirámide Y 64 cm² + 4 × 24 = 160 cm² y para la Pirámide Z 196 ft² + 4 × 77 = 504 ft².
onLevel.instructionsEs: Encuentra el área superficial de cada pirámide cuadrada.
hintsEs: Cada fila necesita dos respuestas: el área de la base cuadrada y luego el área superficial TOTAL (base + 4 triángulos).
Área de la base = arista × arista. Luego suma 4 × (½ × arista × apotema) por las cuatro caras triangulares.
Pirámide X: el área de la base es 12 × 12. Cada triángulo es ½ × 12 × 10: hállalo, multiplícalo por 4 y súmalo a la base.

onLevel.stem: A square pyramid has a base area of 49 cm² and a total lateral area of 84 cm². What is the surface area?
onLevel.explanation: SA = Base Area + Lateral Area = 49 + 84 = 133 cm².
choiceFeedback: That's just the lateral area — add the base area too for total surface area.
That's just the base area — add the lateral (triangular) area too for the total.
Check the units — surface area is measured in square units, not cubic.
hints: Both pieces are already given: base area 49 cm² and lateral (triangle) area 84 cm².
Total surface area = base area + lateral area — one addition, keeping square units.
Set up the sum 49 + 84 and add carefully, keeping cm² in your answer.
onLevel.stemEs: Una pirámide cuadrada tiene un área de base de 49 cm² y un área lateral total de 84 cm². ¿Cuál es el área de superficie?
onLevel.explanationEs: Área de superficie = área de la base + área lateral = 49 + 84 = 133 cm².
hintsEs: Ya te dan las dos piezas: área de la base 49 cm² y área lateral (de los triángulos) 84 cm².
Área superficial total = área de la base + área lateral: una sola suma, conservando las unidades cuadradas.
Plantea la suma 49 + 84 y súmala con cuidado, conservando cm² en tu respuesta.

onLevel.label: A square pyramid has SA = 260 in². The base area is 100 in². What is the total lateral area of the four triangular faces?
onLevel.hint: Subtract the base area from the total surface area to find the lateral area.
hints: The whole bar is the total SA (260 in²), and the base piece (100 in²) is already known.
The lateral faces make up whatever the base doesn't — subtract the base area from the total.
Set up 260 − 100 and find the difference — that's all four triangles together.
onLevel.explanation: The whole bar is the total surface area, 260 in², and it is made of exactly two pieces: the base and the four triangular faces. Since the base piece is 100 in², the lateral piece is what is left, 260 − 100 = 160 in².
onLevel.explanationEs: La barra completa es el área total, 260 in², y está formada por exactamente dos partes: la base y las cuatro caras triangulares. Como la parte de la base es 100 in², la parte lateral es lo que queda: 260 − 100 = 160 in².

onLevel.label: Sort these pyramids from LEAST surface area to GREATEST.
onLevel.hint: Compare each pyramid's surface area and order them.
hints: Each card lists its SA, like 'Base 4×4, slant 5: SA = 56'. Sort using those SA numbers.
Compare only the SA values — notice how a bigger base or a longer slant pushes SA up.
Choose the card with the smallest SA first, then keep picking the next smallest value.
onLevel.explanation: Ordering by the listed totals gives 56, then 96, then 132, then 280. Comparing the middle two shows why: both sit on a 6 × 6 base, but stretching the slant height from 5 to 8 grows every triangular face, so SA climbs from 96 to 132 even though the base never changed.
onLevel.explanationEs: Al ordenar por los totales que aparecen se obtiene 56, luego 96, luego 132 y luego 280. Comparar los dos del medio muestra por qué: ambos están sobre una base de 6 × 6, pero al alargar la altura inclinada de 5 a 8 crece cada cara triangular, así que el área total sube de 96 a 132 aunque la base no cambió.
onLevel.labelEs: Ordena estas pirámides del MENOR área superficial al MAYOR.
hintsEs: Cada tarjeta indica su AS, como 'Base 4×4, apotema 5: AS = 56'. Clasifica usando esos números de AS.
Compara solo los valores de AS y fíjate cómo una base mayor o una apotema más larga sube el AS.
Elige primero la tarjeta con el AS menor y luego sigue eligiendo el siguiente valor más pequeño.

onLevel.title: Did You Halve the Triangle?

workedExample.label: Box
workedExample.work: Square pyramid: base edge = 8 in, slant height = 10 in
workedExample.workEs: Pirámide cuadrada: arista de la base = 8 pulg, altura inclinada = 10 pulg

onLevel.correctWork: A triangle's area is ½ × base × height, so each face is ½ × 8 × 10 = 40 in², not 80 in². The student left out the ½. Four faces: 4 × 40 = 160 in². Correct SA = 64 + 160 = 224 in².
hints: Look at the triangular-face step — what is the area formula for a triangle?
Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height. Each face is ½ × 8 × 10 = 40 in², so SA = 64 + 4 × 40 = 224 in².
onLevel.explanation: The face step multiplied 8 × 10 = 80 in², which is the area of a whole rectangle, not a triangle. A triangle is half of that rectangle, so each face is ½ × 8 × 10 = 40 in², four faces give 160 in², and the correct total is SA = 64 + 160 = 224 in².
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso de la cara multiplicó 8 × 10 = 80 in², que es el área de un rectángulo completo, no de un triángulo. Un triángulo es la mitad de ese rectángulo, así que cada cara es ½ × 8 × 10 = 40 in², cuatro caras dan 160 in² y el total correcto es SA = 64 + 160 = 224 in².
onLevel.correctWorkEs: El área de un triángulo es ½ × base × altura, así que cada cara es ½ × 8 × 10 = 40 in², no 80 in². El estudiante omitió el ½. Cuatro caras: 4 × 40 = 160 in². SA correcta = 64 + 160 = 224 in².

extending.title: Find the Surface Area Error

workedExample.label: Dimensions
workedExample.work: Square pyramid: base edge = 10 in, slant height = 8 in
workedExample.workEs: Pirámide cuadrada: arista de la base = 10 pulg, altura inclinada = 8 pulg

workedExample.label: Lateral Area
workedExample.work: ½ × 10 × 8 = 40 in² (one face). Total lateral = 40 × 3 = 120 in²
workedExample.workEs: ½ × 10 × 8 = 40 in² (una cara). Lateral total = 40 × 3 = 120 in²

extending.correctWork: A square pyramid has 4 lateral faces, not 3. Total lateral = 40 × 4 = 160 in². Correct: SA = 100 + 160 = 260 in².
hints: Check Step 3: how many lateral faces does a square pyramid have?
A square base has 4 sides, so there are 4 triangular faces. The student only multiplied by 3.
extending.titleEs: Encuentra el error de área total
extending.explanation: The area of one face, ½ × 10 × 8 = 40 in², is right, but it was multiplied by 3 instead of 4. A square base has four sides, so four triangles meet at the top: 40 × 4 = 160 in², and SA = 100 + 160 = 260 in².
extending.explanationEs: El área de una cara, ½ × 10 × 8 = 40 in², está bien, pero se multiplicó por 3 en vez de por 4. Una base cuadrada tiene cuatro lados, así que cuatro triángulos se juntan en la punta: 40 × 4 = 160 in², y SA = 100 + 160 = 260 in².
extending.correctWorkEs: Una pirámide cuadrada tiene 4 caras laterales, no 3. Lateral total = 40 × 4 = 160 in². Correcto: SA = 100 + 160 = 260 in².

extending.prompt: Two pyramids have the same base area (64 in²) but different slant heights. Pyramid A has slant height 6 in and Pyramid B has slant height 10 in. How much more surface area does Pyramid B have? Why does slant height affect surface area but NOT base area?
extending.sentenceFrame: Pyramid A: SA = 64 + 4(½ × 8 × 6) = 64 + ___ = ___ in². Pyramid B: SA = 64 + 4(½ × 8 × 10) = 64 + ___ = ___ in². Pyramid B has ___ more in² because ___. Slant height only affects ___ because ___.
extending.hint: Find each pyramid's surface area, then compare the totals.
hints: Both pyramids share a 64 in² base (edge 8 in). Only the slant heights differ: 6 in versus 10 in.
Find each SA = 64 + 4 × (½ × 8 × slant height), then subtract the totals. The base never uses the slant height.
Pyramid A first: one triangle is ½ × 8 × 6. Multiply by 4, add 64, then repeat using slant height 10.
extending.explanation: With a 64 in² base the edge is 8 in, so Pyramid A has SA = 64 + 4(½ × 8 × 6) = 64 + 96 = 160 in² and Pyramid B has SA = 64 + 4(½ × 8 × 10) = 64 + 160 = 224 in², a difference of 64 in². Slant height only appears in the triangle formula, so it stretches the lateral faces while the base area stays 8 × 8 no matter how tall the pyramid gets.
extending.explanationEs: Con una base de 64 in² la arista mide 8 in, así que la Pirámide A tiene SA = 64 + 4(½ × 8 × 6) = 64 + 96 = 160 in² y la Pirámide B tiene SA = 64 + 4(½ × 8 × 10) = 64 + 160 = 224 in², una diferencia de 64 in². La altura inclinada solo aparece en la fórmula del triángulo, así que estira las caras laterales mientras el área de la base sigue siendo 8 × 8 sin importar cuánto suba la pirámide.
extending.promptEs: Dos pirámides tienen la misma área de base (64 in²) pero alturas inclinadas diferentes. La pirámide A tiene una altura inclinada de 6 in y la pirámide B de 10 in. ¿Cuánta área superficial más tiene la pirámide B? ¿Por qué la altura inclinada afecta el área superficial pero NO el área de la base?
hintsEs: Ambas pirámides comparten una base de 64 pulg² (arista de 8 pulg). Solo cambian las apotemas: 6 pulg frente a 10 pulg.
Halla cada AS = 64 + 4 × (½ × 8 × apotema) y luego resta los totales. La base nunca usa la apotema.
Pirámide A primero: un triángulo es ½ × 8 × 6. Multiplica por 4, suma 64 y luego repite con la apotema de 10.

extending.instructions: Compare a square pyramid and a rectangular prism that sit on the same 6 × 6 base.
extending.hint: Find each shape's base area(s), side area, and total surface area.
hints: Both shapes sit on a 6 × 6 base, but the pyramid has 4 triangles while the prism has 4 rectangles and TWO square bases.
Pyramid lateral: 4 × (½ × 6 × 8). Prism lateral: 4 × (6 × 8). Then add each shape's base area(s).
Pyramid first: one triangle is ½ × 6 × 8 = 24. Multiply by 4 for the lateral area, then add the 36 base.
extending.explanation: On the same 6 × 6 base, the pyramid's four triangles give 4 × (½ × 6 × 8) = 96, so its total is 36 + 96 = 132. The prism's four sides are full rectangles, 4 × (6 × 8) = 192, and it has two bases, so its total is 72 + 192 = 264 — the prism needs exactly twice the material because its sides are not halved and it has a top.
extending.explanationEs: Sobre la misma base de 6 × 6, los cuatro triángulos de la pirámide dan 4 × (½ × 6 × 8) = 96, así que su total es 36 + 96 = 132. Los cuatro lados del prisma son rectángulos completos, 4 × (6 × 8) = 192, y tiene dos bases, así que su total es 72 + 192 = 264: el prisma necesita exactamente el doble de material porque sus lados no se dividen a la mitad y además tiene tapa.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Surface Area of Pyramids is finding the four triangular lateral faces correctly (½ × base edge × slant height, times 4) and then stopping — forgetting to add the base area at the end. This leaves the total surface area too small by exactly the base's area. Before you submit, ask: 'Did I add the base area to the four lateral faces, or did I stop after the sides?'

diagram.title: Glass Faces of the Display Case
diagram.caption: Each bar is one face's area in ft²; the open base adds 0 and the four triangular faces (½×3×4 = 6 ft² each) add up to 24 ft² of glass.

connect.scenario: A museum is building a square pyramid display case. The base edge is 3 feet and the slant height is 4 feet. The glass costs $12 per square foot.
connect.promptQuestion: How much will the glass for all 4 triangular sides cost? (The base is open — no glass needed.)
connect.prompt: Each triangular face has area = ½ × ___ × ___ = ___ ft². Four faces: 4 × ___ = ___ ft². Cost: ___ × $12 = $___.

check.stem: What is the area of one triangular face?
check.explanation: A = ½ × base × slant height = ½ × 3 × 4 = 6 ft².

check.stem: What is the total glass area for all four faces?
check.explanation: 4 × 6 = 24 ft². The base is open, so it adds 0.

connect.modelAnswer: Each triangular face is ½ × 3 × 4 = 6 ft², and there are 4 of them: 4 × 6 = 24 ft² of glass (the base is open, so it needs none). At $12 per square foot the glass costs 24 × $12 = $288.

exitTicket.stem: A square pyramid has a base edge of 6 in and a slant height of 5 in. What is the total surface area?
exitTicket.explanation: Base: 6 × 6 = 36 in². Each lateral face: ½ × 6 × 5 = 15 in². Four faces: 4 × 15 = 60 in². SA = 36 + 60 = 96 in². Surface area uses square units (in²).
choiceFeedback: Add the base area too — total surface is base plus 4 triangles.
Surface area is square units (in²), not cubic.
That's only the base — include the four triangular faces.
hints: Two parts make the total: a 6 × 6 square base plus 4 triangles with base 6 and slant height 5.
SA = base area + 4 × (½ × base edge × slant height). Don't stop after the triangles — include the base.
Base: 6 × 6 = 36 in². One triangle: ½ × 6 × 5. Find it, multiply by 4, then add to the base area.
